newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's Sanfu to join Burma car project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's Sanfu to join Burma car project.

text.p: Taiwan's Sanfu Motors said on Tuesday it planned to form a US$50-100 million joint venture with the Burmese government to build a car manufacturing plant in Rangoon.

The project, if approved by Taiwan's investment commission, would make passenger cars designed by Sanfu and would begin production in the third quarter of 1998 at a monthly capacity of 400 cars, a Sanfu spokesman said.
"We will submit a formal application with the investment commission very soon," he said by telephone.
Sanfu said it would seek other Taiwan firms to take up a combined 60-percent stake in the project. Burma's government and state-run firms would account for the remaining 40 percent.
"We do not know the exact investment breakdown right now, nor have we finalised who the other investors will be," the Sanfu spokesman, who declined to be named, said.
He said Sanfu decided to participate in the project because of an expected rise in demand for cars in Burma.
"Burma has a population of 45 million, and our feasibility study suggests that automobile consumption is on a sharp rise," he said.
